title: Wisdom Is Currency
subtitle: The Principle
verse: "Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding."
teaching:
Everybody's chasing the money....

But money's downstream.

Track it backwards with me. The money came from somebody solving a problem. The solution came from an idea. The idea came from wisdom. So the money you want? It's four steps down the river from *wisdom*. Most people spend their whole life splashing around at the bottom of the river, wondering why they can't catch anything — when the source is upstream.

Here's the reframe that changes everything: **wisdom is currency.** It's spendable. It's investable. You can earn it, and you can lose it. It's not a nice quote for the wall — it's a *resource*. And the Book calls it "the principal thing" — the *first* thing, the *seed*. Get that, and you get everything it produces.

For the next 7 days, you're going upstream.
work:
- Write this down where you'll see it: *"For the next 7 days, I'm going after wisdom first."*
- Name the excuse that usually stops you (too busy, too tired, "I'll start Monday") — write it down, and decide it doesn't get a vote this week.
- Pick your daily time block for the challenge (tomorrow you'll use it). Morning is best — first, not leftover.
journal: Where have I been chasing the money instead of the wisdom that produces it? What changes if I flip that order?

title: Worth More Than Gold
subtitle: The Value
verse: "Happy is the man that findeth wisdom... for the merchandise of it is better than the merchandise of silver, and the gain thereof than fine gold."
teaching:
Yesterday you learned *what* wisdom is. Today, *what it's worth* — because you'll never pursue something you've underpriced.

The Book puts wisdom's return *above* silver and gold. Not equal to — *better than*. Think about that. The thing everybody's killing themselves to get, God says wisdom out-earns it.

But here's the deeper cut, and I need you to sit with it: **you are the asset the wisdom flows through.** Fearfully and wonderfully made. There's a way of seeing, a story, a gift in you that nobody else on earth carries. Most people undervalue *two* things at once — the wisdom, and themselves — so they end up building a generic version of a generic life.

Today we raise your valuation. Of wisdom. And of you.
work:
- Part 1: List **3 times** wisdom — a right call, a caught red flag, an insight — saved or made you more than money ever could.
- Part 2: List **3 things that make you YOU** — your lane, your story, your gift. The raw material God wants to multiply.
journal: If I truly believed my wisdom and my uniqueness were my greatest assets — what would I stop doing? What would I start?
anchor: You're not behind. You're undervalued — including to yourself.

title: The Tithe of Time
subtitle: The Covenant
verse: "Honour the Lord with... the firstfruits of all thine increase."
teaching:
This is the engine. Everything else spins off of today.

Years ago, 3:30 in the morning, I heard it plain: *master time the way a believer masters money — through the tithe.* Give God the firstfruits of your time, and He'll show you the secrets to leveraging the rest.

Firstfruits. Not the leftover minutes at the end of a drained day. The *first*. Before the phone, before the noise, before the world starts pulling on you. When you give Him the first of your time, He gives you the first of His wisdom.

And hear me — this isn't a transaction. It's a *covenant*. It flows out of relationship, not a vending machine. You're not paying for wisdom; you're sitting with the One who gives it. The prayer and the Word open the door. But don't rush out — **the listening is where the download comes.**

Today, you start.
work:
- Do your first tithe-of-time session **today**. Use the block you picked on Day 1.
- Structure it: *quiet the noise → a short prayer asking for wisdom (James 1:5) → read a few verses → then SIT and listen, with your capture tool open.*
- Short on time? 20–30 focused minutes counts — as long as it's firstfruits, not scraps.
journal: What currently owns the first part of my morning? What has to move so God gets the firstfruits?
anchor: Give Him the first, not the leftover.

title: Catch the Download
subtitle: The Capture
verse: "Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it."
teaching:
Here's where most people leak — and never even know it.

You give God the time. The wisdom comes — an idea, a nudge, a solution to something that's had you stuck, a verse that hits different. And then... by lunch... it's gone. Evaporated. You had gold in your hand and you let it run through your fingers because you trusted your memory.

The wise don't trust their memory. They **capture.**

Look at the scripture — God didn't say *remember* the vision. He said *write* it. Make it plain. A captured idea is an *asset*. An uncaptured one is a blessing that knocked, waited, and left because nobody answered the door.

Today you build the habit that most people never do — and it changes everything.
work:
- Set up **one** capture place — notes app, a voice-memo folder, a physical journal. *One.* Always on you.
- Go back through yesterday's session and capture everything that came up.
- Then carry it all day and log **every** idea, nudge, or thought — no editing, no judging. Aim for **5–10 captures** by tonight. Today is quantity, not quality.
journal: How many ideas have I lost this year because I never wrote them down? What is my ONE capture place, starting now?
anchor: An idea you don't capture is a blessing you decline.

title: Sift for the Gold
subtitle: Discernment
verse: "If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally... and it shall be given him."
teaching:
Now you've got raw material — a pile of captures. Some of it's noise. Some of it's gold. Today you learn the difference.

Because not every idea is *the* idea. And knowing which seed to plant? That's wisdom itself — so you *ask* for it. You don't force the answer; you discern it. You bring the pile to God and say, "Which one of these has Your hand on it?"

Look for the idea with **weight**. You'll know it — it's the one that keeps coming back. The one that lines up with who you are (remember Day 2 — your lane, your gift). The one that solves a real problem for real people, and stirs something in you when you look at it. That pull is not an accident.
work:
- Read back through *all* your captures.
- Pray Day's scripture — ask God for wisdom to see clearly.
- Mark the **1–3** ideas with the most pull: keeps returning + fits your lane + solves a real problem.
- Now circle the **ONE** with the most weight. That's your seed.
journal: Which idea keeps knocking? Which one aligns with the asset that is *me*? Why that one?
anchor: Discernment is just wisdom applied to your options.

title: Write the Vision
subtitle: The Shape
verse: "Write the vision, and make it plain... For the vision is yet for an appointed time... though it tarry, wait for it; it will surely come."
teaching:
You've got the one idea. Today you give it a body.

A vision in your head is fog — it feels big, but you can't grab it, can't move on it, can't hand it to anybody. A vision *on paper* is a plan. Look at the scripture again: "make it plain, that he may **run**." Plain enough to run. That's the goal today — not fancy, not finished. *Workable.* Workable means you can start.

Don't overcomplicate it. One page. What is it, who's it for, what does it solve, what's the simplest first version. That's it. The fog becomes a direction the moment your pen hits the paper.

And that line at the end of the verse — *"though it tarry, wait for it; it will surely come"* — hold onto that. Your vision might be for an appointed time. Writing it plain is how you're ready when the fullness of time hits.
work:
Draft your **one-page Workable Vision.** Answer plainly:
1. **What is it?** (one sentence)
2. **Who is it for?**
3. **What problem does it solve / what does it produce?**
4. **What's the simplest first version** I could put into the world?
5. **Why me? Why now?**

Keep it to one page. Plain beats fancy every time.
journal: If I had to explain this vision to a friend in 30 seconds, what would I say? Is it plain enough to *run* with?
anchor: A vision on paper is the difference between a dream and a direction.

title: Faith With Works
subtitle: The First Step
verse: "Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone."
teaching:
The vision is written. But watch this — a written vision that never *moves* is still just a nicer daydream. Faith without works is dead. The idea was never the finish line; the *execution* is.

So today, you put your hands on it. Not the whole thing — that'll overwhelm you and you'll freeze. *One step.* The first domino. Small enough that you can't talk yourself out of it.

And then — this is the part most people miss — you keep the cycle **spinning**. This whole week was one lap of the flywheel: you gave the time, you got the wisdom, you caught the ideas, you shaped the vision. The magic isn't doing it once. It's *keeping it turning*. The tithe of time continues. The capture continues. The wisdom keeps flowing, the vision keeps growing.

You came in chasing money. You're leaving with something better — a system that produces it, and a vision worth building.
work:
- Define the **ONE first step** that moves your vision from paper to motion — small enough to do in the **next 48 hours.**
- Do it now, or schedule it right now.
- **Commit to keeping the covenant** — put your tithe-of-time block on the calendar as a standing, recurring appointment. This is the part that changes your life, not just your week.
- *(Optional, powerful):* share your vision and first step publicly. Accountability — and it just might bless somebody watching.
journal: What is the ONE step I can take in the next 48 hours? And will I keep the covenant going after today?
anchor: The wise don't just receive the vision. They work it.
